title: Elasticity structure of medicinal taxa by growth form (harvest-vulnerability screening)
question: Do medicinal trees/long-lived perennials have higher survival-stasis elasticity than short-lived herbs, implying adult/organ harvest is riskier?
hypothesis: Median stasis elasticity: trees > perennials > short-lived; fecundity elasticity the reverse (Kruskal-Wallis p<0.05), one value per species (not per matrix).
data: COMPADRE medicinal taxa, unmanipulated mean/pooled matrices passing QC
finding: Median stasis elasticity: woody 0.857, herbaceous perennial 0.486, annual 0.005 (Kruskal-Wallis p=4.3e-12); fecundity elasticity reverses. Used only as a qualitative screening flag for species without harvest experiments; descriptive, species-level, not phylogenetically corrected.

result.screening_rule: If species-level survival elasticity (stasis+progression+retrogression) >= 0.8, flag harvest of established plants/organs as high-sensitivity; do not infer a rate.
